parts.title: Part 1

passage.title: Cycling and knees
passage.content:
Cycling keeps us fit and healthy. It is good for our heart and our mental health. It also keeps our weight down. A surprising benefit of getting on a bike is that it is good for our knees. A new study says cyclists have less knee pain when they get older. The _____ is from Baylor College of Medicine in the USA. Researchers surveyed 2,600 people, with an average age of 64. The _____ were asked about their levels of physical activity. They also had X-rays of their knees taken. _____ looked at the X-rays for signs of arthritis in the knee joints.

Lead researcher Dr Grace Lo was surprised by the results of the research. She said _____ were 21 per cent less likely to have signs of a joint problem called osteoarthritis. This is often called "wear-and-tear" arthritis. It happens when we use our joints a lot. The joint wears down and becomes painful. _____ is a very common disease. It usually starts when people are in their fifties. Dr Lo said cycling, "is a great preventative strategy for many things, including arthritis". A lot of _____ shows that cyclists are around 20 per cent less likely to die prematurely.

parts.instruction: Read the text. Fill in each gap with ONE word. You must use a word which is somewhere in the rest of the text.

q1.text: The previous sentence introduces a "new study". The sentence with the gap then gives the source of this study, which is Baylor College of Medicine. That's why the correct answer is 'study'.
q1.quote: A new study says cyclists have less knee pain when they get older.

q2.text: The text states that researchers surveyed 2,600 people. The sentence with the gap describes what these individuals were asked about their physical activity. That's why the correct answer is 'people'.
q2.quote: Researchers surveyed 2,600 people, with an average age of 64.

q3.text: The passage mentions that researchers surveyed people and that X-rays were taken. It is the job of the researchers to analyze the data, including the X-rays. That's why the correct answer is 'researchers'.
q3.quote: Researchers surveyed 2,600 people, with an average age of 64.

q4.text: The study is about the benefits of cycling. The lead researcher is explaining the results, which showed that people who cycle had fewer signs of a specific joint problem. That's why the correct answer is 'cyclists'.
q4.quote: A new study says cyclists have less knee pain when they get older.

q5.text: The previous sentences describe a joint problem called osteoarthritis, which is also known as "wear-and-tear" arthritis. The sentence with the gap gives more information about this condition. That's why the correct answer is 'arthritis'.

q6.text: The final sentence presents another general finding about the benefits of cycling. The phrase "A lot of..." followed by "shows" indicates a body of evidence or investigation. That's why the correct answer is 'research'.
q6.quote: Lead researcher Dr Grace Lo was surprised by the results of the research.

parts.title: Part 3

paragraphs.content: Today Jakarta has much to offer, ranging from museums, art and antique markets, first class shopping to accommodations and a wide variety of cultural activities. Jakarta's most famous landmark, the National Monument or Monas, is a 137m obelisk topped with a flame sculpture coated with 35 kg of gold. Other attractions include the National Museum with ethnographic artifacts and the Maritime Museum exhibiting Indonesia's seafaring traditions.

Sumatra is a paradise for nature lovers, with national parks, mountains and coastlines suited to adventure. Along western shores there are strong waves that attract surfers, while coral reefs provide excellent diving. Night divers can explore the waters around islands in the Riau Archipelago and encounter unusual marine creatures in the dark.

Many establishments offer complete pampering services with floral baths, body scrubs, aromatic oils, massages and meditation. Ritual treatments use herbs and spices to promote both physical and mental wellness. Indonesians are known for treating the body and mind as a connected whole.

Jakarta has a distinctly cosmopolitan flavor. You can enjoy food from local eateries to stylish cafes and international restaurants. The taste of Indonesia's many cultures can be found throughout the city, from spicy dishes of West Sumatra to sweet flavors associated with Central Java.

Despite modernization and strong foreign influence, many native communities maintain their rituals, architecture, religion, dance and music. On islands such as Siberut, tribal groups still preserve long-standing communal traditions and ceremonial practices that reflect pre-modern heritage.

Whether you are a serious spender or a casual shopper, Jakarta offers choices for every budget. You can find local handicrafts, modern fashion labels, shopping centers, quality goods at competitive prices and lively sidewalk bargains ranging from flowers to tropical fruits.

parts.title: Part 4

passage.title: The Cacao
passage.content:
Most people today think of chocolate as something sweet to eat or drink that can be easily found in stores around the world. It might surprise you that chocolate was once highly treasured. Historians believe the Maya people of Central America first learned to farm cacao plants around two thousand years ago. They cooked cacao seeds, crushed them into a soft paste and mixed it with water and spices to make an unsweetened drink. The Maya poured the drink between containers so it developed a layer of bubbles.

Cacao and chocolate were an important part of Maya culture. Ruling families drank chocolate at special ceremonies, and even poorer members of society could enjoy it only from time to time. Historians also believe cacao seeds were connected with marriage ceremonies. In Aztec culture around present-day Mexico, cacao plants could not grow easily in the area where many Aztecs lived, so they traded for cacao. Aztec rulers used cacao seeds as a form of money to pay taxes. Priests offered cacao to the gods and served chocolate in sacred events.

The explorer Christopher Columbus brought cacao seeds to Spain after his trip to Central America in 1502, but Spanish explorer Hernando Cortes later understood cacao's economic potential. After the Spanish defeated the Aztec empire, they seized cacao supplies and sent them home. Spain later expanded cacao growing in American colonies to meet rising demand.

At first, wealthy people in Spain enjoyed a sweetened chocolate drink. Later, chocolate spread through Europe. Because of price, only rich people could afford it until the eighteenth century. During the Industrial Revolution, new technologies made chocolate less costly to produce. Farmers then grew cacao trees in many countries in Africa, Central America and South America.

Cacao trees need heat, water, shade, suitable soil and protection, so farming can be difficult. Trees begin producing pods after several years, and seeds from these pods are harvested to make chocolate. Farm cacao trees can be more vulnerable to disease and insects than wild trees, and uncertain market conditions can reduce farmers' income. In modern production, cacao seeds are sorted, cleaned and cooked. Workers break and crush the seeds into chocolate liquor, then separate solids and cocoa butter. Manufacturers blend chocolate liquor with sugar, milk and cocoa fat before further processing and molding.

passage.title: Safety Measures for Roof Work
passage.content:
Roof work is inherently dangerous, involving activities at significant heights and often under challenging conditions. To reduce the risks associated with this type of work, it is essential to implement comprehensive safety measures. These measures are designed to protect workers from falls, equipment failures and adverse weather, ensuring a safer working environment.

One of the foremost concerns in roof work is the risk of falls. Personal protective equipment is crucial in minimizing this risk. Workers must wear harnesses that are correctly fitted and regularly inspected for wear and tear. Helmets are also essential, providing protection against falling objects and reducing the risk of head injuries. Non-slip footwear helps prevent slips on roofing materials, especially when surfaces are wet or icy.

Structural safety measures are equally important. Safety nets and guardrails are two key methods of fall prevention. Safety nets installed below the working area can catch workers if they fall, preventing serious injury. Guardrails provide a physical barrier around the perimeter of the roof and prevent workers from stepping over the edge. Both systems must meet regulatory standards and undergo regular checks.

Access to the roof is another critical aspect of safety. Ladders and scaffolding are commonly used to reach high areas. These tools must be placed on stable ground and inspected for defects before use. Scaffolding should be properly braced and capable of supporting workers and materials. Ladders should extend at least three feet above the roof edge to provide a secure handhold while workers transition between ladder and roof.

Weather conditions play a major role in roof safety. High winds, heavy rain and icy conditions can create hazardous working environments. It is crucial to monitor forecasts and avoid roof work during dangerous weather. Scheduling tasks in favorable weather can significantly reduce accident risk.

Training and supervision are vital for maintaining safety standards. Workers need instruction on safe work practices, correct equipment use and emergency procedures. Regular briefings and drills keep safety protocols fresh. Supervisors should ensure adherence to guidelines and respond quickly to any hazards. Effective communication, including radios or other devices, helps teams stay coordinated and prevents misunderstandings that can lead to accidents.

Proper planning and risk assessment are critical before work begins. A thorough assessment should identify hazards, define mitigation strategies, confirm equipment condition, specify safe access points and develop contingency plans for emergencies.
